overview: Bank of Communications (BOCOM), founded in 1908 and headquartered in Shanghai, is the fifth-largest of China's state-owned commercial banks (the smallest of the 'big six' alongside ICBC, CCB, ABC, BOC and PSBC) and a designated global systemically important bank. It provides full-service corporate and retail banking, wealth management, treasury, trade finance and investment banking through roughly 2,800 domestic outlets, 24 overseas branches/subsidiaries, and a growing suite of financial-license subsidiaries (leasing, fund management, trust, insurance, overseas securities). The bank is dual-listed (A-shares on the SSE, H-shares on HKEX) and reports in RMB with total assets of RMB15.5 trillion at end-FY2025.

business_model.summary: BOCOM earns the large majority of revenue from net interest income on a RMB15.5tn balance sheet of loans, bonds and interbank assets funded by customer deposits, supplemented by net fee and commission income from wealth management, cards, settlement and agency services, and treasury/trading income. Margins are thin but the model is highly recurring (interest income re-prices continuously on a large, stable deposit-funded book) rather than transactional or project-based.

revenue_streams.name: Net fee and commission income
revenue_streams.trend: pressured by wealth-management fee cuts, slowly recovering

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B and B2C: 3.17 million corporate customers (large SOEs, infrastructure, SMEs) and 208 million retail customers (mortgages, credit cards, consumer loans, wealth management/private banking)
business_model.geographic_mix: Domestic China ~96% of loans (Yangtze River Delta ~29%, Bohai Rim ~16%, Central China ~16%, Pearl River Delta ~13%, Western China ~12%, overseas ~3.6%), with Shanghai as strategic 'home base'; overseas branches/subsidiaries in Hong Kong and other international centers

main_competitors: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
competitive_position.market_position: Smallest of China's 'big six' state-owned commercial banks by assets, ranked 9th globally by tier-1 capital (The Banker, 2025); a Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) since 2023; the China's big six collectively hold roughly 40%+ of national banking-sector assets

moat_factors.factor: State ownership and implicit government backing
moat_factors.description: Majority state-owned (Ministry of Finance is largest shareholder), conferring an implicit sovereign backstop, access to policy lending programs and PBOC liquidity facilities, and strong funding-cost advantages over joint-stock and city/rural banks
RMB9.3tn+ customer deposit base and RMB15.5tn balance sheet create a low, stable cost of funds difficult for smaller banks to replicate
Chinese banking licensing, capital and branch-network requirements heavily favor incumbents; new entrants face high regulatory hurdles
Headquartered in Shanghai with privileged access to the city's 'five centers' financial-market infrastructure (RMB internationalization, offshore/cross-border finance, clearing and settlement)
118-year history, first nationwide state-owned joint-stock bank; recognized brand but less retail mindshare than ICBC/CCB/ABC at the mass-market level

weaknesses: Smallest of the big six, with less scale-driven cost efficiency and weaker retail deposit market share than ICBC/CCB/ABC
Lowest net interest margin among domestic peers (1.20% FY2025) reflecting a more wholesale/corporate-funded balance sheet
Credit-card and personal unsecured loan quality weaker than mortgage book, with credit-card NPL ratio of 2.68% and high (10.4%) NPL ratio in accommodation/catering sector loans
Heavier reliance on recent capital raises (large placement) rather than organic capital generation to support loan growth
Thinner profitability (ROE ~8.4% FY2025, declining) versus the largest state banks

growth_drivers: Deposit repricing tailwind: large back-book of 3-year time deposits maturing and rolling over at lower rates is expected to add ~10-12bp to sector NIM through 2026-2027, partially offsetting asset-side yield declines

'Five priorities' policy-directed lending (technology finance, green finance, inclusive finance, ageing finance, digital finance) now ~1/3 of total loan book, with technology loans >16% and green/inclusive loans >10% each — a structural growth channel aligned with state policy and PBOC relending facilities
Wealth management and AUM growth: retail wealth management AUM reached RMB2.16 trillion (+10% YoY), with cumulative five-year AUM growth of 30.6%, supporting higher-margin, capital-light fee income
Shanghai 'home base' strategy and offshore/cross-border RMB business, leveraging Shanghai's development as a global RMB asset-allocation and risk-management center
AI and digital transformation ('AI+' initiative) aimed at cost efficiency (cost-to-income ratio already improved to 29.3% in FY2025 and 27.5% in H1 2026) and enhanced risk/fraud detection
Consolidation of controlled rural banks (Dayi, Laoshan, Anji, Shihezi) into branches, simplifying structure and capturing full economics of previously minority-owned units
Three-key-region loan concentration strategy (Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, Bay Area) now ~54% of loans, targeting China's highest-growth regional economies

business.description: Real estate loans are RMB515bn (5.65% of total loans) with an elevated NPL ratio of 4.20% (improved from 4.85% a year earlier); exposure is being actively worked down but the sector downturn continues to pressure collateral values and borrower repayment capacity, and local-government-debt-linked exposures are flagged by management as a key area requiring continued monitoring and resolution

business.risk: Retail / personal loan asset quality deterioration
business.description: Personal loan NPL ratio rose to 1.58% (from lower levels), credit card NPL ratio 2.68%, consumption loan NPL ratio ~1.77%; management explicitly flags this as a 'major concern of capital market' consistent with industry-wide retail credit stress
Lower NIM and less retail deposit stickiness than larger peers constrain profitability and competitive responses to margin pressure

financial.description: NIM has fallen from 1.56% (FY2021) to 1.20% (FY2025), driven by LPR cuts, asset re-pricing and mortgage rate reductions outpacing deposit cost declines; though H1 2026 showed a modest NIM uptick to 1.23% as deposit repricing tailwinds begin to help, the multi-year compression has been the dominant driver of ROE decline (10.76% FY2021 to 8.38% FY2025, and down further to 8.09% in H1 2026)

Completed a RMB~120bn (net RMB119.9bn) private placement of ~14.1bn new A-shares in mid-2025, mostly to the Ministry of Finance with China National Tobacco Corporation (CNTC) and China Shuangwei Investment (CDIC) as co-subscribers, expanding total ordinary shares outstanding from ~74.26bn to ~88.36bn (a ~19% increase); FY2025 EPS fell to RMB1.08 from RMB1.16 in FY2024 despite net profit growth of 2.18%, and H1 2026 EPS fell 11.9% YoY on a larger share base — a clear and quantifiable dilution drag on per-share metrics even as the capital injection improved core tier-1 ratio to 11.43%

Provision coverage ratio has been declining modestly from its FY2025 peak of 208.4% to 203.8% at H1 2026, alongside a slight uptick in NPL ratio (1.28% to 1.30%), bearing watching as a leading indicator of credit cost trajectory

regulatory.description: As a state-owned G-SIB, BOCOM is expected to support national priorities (technology innovation, green transition, inclusive finance, regional development strategies) which can direct capital toward policy objectives rather than purely risk-adjusted returns, and the bank must maintain capital and liquidity buffers per NFRA/PBOC macroprudential rules

regulatory.risk: Global systemically important bank (G-SIB) capital surcharge
regulatory.description: G-SIB designation (since 2023) imposes additional capital buffer requirements, raising the bar for capital management and potentially necessitating further equity or capital-instrument issuance over time

regulatory.risk: Government ownership and minority shareholder alignment
regulatory.description: Ministry of Finance as controlling shareholder (further increased via the 2025 placement) raises governance questions around whether capital allocation and dividend policy always align with minority (particularly H-share/foreign) shareholder interests

macro.risk: China GDP growth slowdown / credit demand softness
macro.description: China's GDP grew 4.7% YoY in H1 2026; continued deceleration in real estate and broader credit demand could further pressure loan growth and asset quality

As a deposit-funded lender, BOCOM's NIM and net interest income are highly sensitive to PBOC policy rate cuts, LPR reductions and deposit rate ceilings; further accommodative monetary policy to support the economy could continue to squeeze margins even as deposit repricing offers some offset

macro.risk: RMB currency and capital account policy
macro.description: Cross-border and offshore RMB business exposes the bank to RMB exchange rate and capital-control policy shifts, though this is a smaller share of the overall book

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's big state-owned banks are expected to see net profit growth resume and NIM stabilize in 2026-2027 as deposit repricing offsets asset-yield declines; sector net interest income for listed banks is projected to rise ~8.4% YoY with state-owned banks' revenue up ~9.4%, though individual banks (e.g., Bank of China) still report ongoing NIM declines, so the pace of stabilization varies by bank
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical — credit growth, asset quality and fee income (wealth management, investment banking) track the domestic economic cycle, property market health and equity/bond market conditions; counter-cyclical policy lending partially smooths volatility
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — NIM and net interest income are the dominant profit driver and move directly with PBOC policy rates, LPR resets and deposit cost trends
key_input_costs: Regulatory capital costs (additional tier-1, tier-2 instruments)

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 interim results: net operating income RMB142.5bn (+6.77% YoY), net profit attributable to shareholders RMB47.9bn (+4.04% YoY), but EPS fell 11.9% YoY to RMB0.52 due to the enlarged post-placement share base; NIM ticked up to 1.23% (from 1.21%), NPL ratio edged up to 1.30%, provision coverage eased to 203.80%, CET1 ratio declined to 11.25%

FY2025 annual results: total assets RMB15.5tn (+4.35%), operating income RMB265.6bn (+2.02%), net profit RMB95.6bn (+2.18%), NIM compressed further to 1.20% (from 1.27%), but asset quality improved — NPL ratio down to 1.28% (best in recent years) and provision coverage up to 208.4%; core tier-1 ratio rose to 11.43% post-placement; dividend payout ratio maintained above 30% for the 14th consecutive year

Completed the RMB~120bn (net RMB119.9bn) A-share private placement — 14.1bn new shares issued at RMB8.51/share to the Ministry of Finance (~RMB13.2bn), China National Tobacco Corporation (~RMB538m) and China Shuangwei Investment/CDIC (~RMB353m) — to shore up core tier-1 capital; total ordinary shares outstanding rose from ~74.26bn to ~88.36bn (~19% dilution)

Completed conversion of four BOCOM-controlled rural banks (Dayi, Laoshan, Anji, Shihezi) into direct branches as part of the national small/medium financial institution 'reform and risk resolution' initiative

Board of Directors change completed (new 11th Session board), described by the Chairman as 'injecting fresh impetus' into corporate governance; wealth management AUM grew to RMB2.16tn (+10% YoY) amid product innovation (e.g., gold-accumulation product 'Tun Jin Bao') and AI-assisted advisory tools

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report / FY2025 Annual Report Outlook sections

items.notes: Management states it will grow light-capital/intermediary businesses (wealth management, investment banking, transaction banking, custody) while 'maintaining overall stability of its net interest margin'; no specific numeric NIM target disclosed

14th consecutive year of >30% payout ratio; FY2025 total dividend RMB3.247 per 10 shares (including interim); H1 2026 interim dividend of RMB0.168/share representing 31.0% of H1 net profit, consistent with policy continuation

items.target: continue expanding technology (>16% of loans), green and inclusive loans (each >10%) as share of total lending
items.notes: No specific numeric target disclosed beyond qualitative commitment to further escalate intensity and alignment of lending to these state policy priorities

items.target: maintain provisioning coverage above regulatory requirements and potential risk levels; continue intensive disposal of real estate and local-government-debt-linked risk
items.notes: Qualitative guidance only; no explicit NPL ratio or coverage ratio target provided

items.target: no further specific capital-raising target disclosed post-2025 placement
items.notes: Core tier-1 ratio at 11.43% (FY2025) eased slightly to 11.25% (H1 2026) as RWA growth continues to absorb the capital injection; management did not guide to a new placement but continues to emphasize capital discipline amid G-SIB buffer requirements

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Ren Deqi characterized FY2025 as a year in which 'operating results exceeded expectations, and all business development targets set by the Board of Directors were achieved,' crediting the RMB120bn placement with 'further consolidating the foundation for medium to long-term development.' Management's FY2026 outlook (opening of the 15th Five-Year Plan period) emphasizes continuing the 'five priorities' of finance, advancing an 'AI+' action plan to cut costs and improve efficiency, strengthening the customer base (mid-size and small customer acquisition), deepening the Shanghai 'home base' strategy, and 'securing the bottom line of preventing systematic risks' with continued focus on resolving real estate and local-government-debt risk exposures.

bull_case: Deep value / high yield: trades at roughly 7x trailing earnings with a near-5% dividend yield and a payout ratio maintained above 30% for 14 consecutive years, appealing for income-focused investors

NIM stabilization tailwind: industry-wide deposit repricing (maturing high-cost 3-year deposits rolling over at much lower rates) is expected to add back 10-12bp of margin across China's big banks through 2026-2027, and BOCOM's H1 2026 NIM already ticked up for the first time in several years

Freshly recapitalized balance sheet: the RMB120bn placement lifted core tier-1 capital to 11.43%+ (among the strongest in the bank's history), providing headroom for loan growth and absorbing further credit costs without near-term dilutive follow-on raises

Improving asset quality: NPL ratio at 1.28-1.30% is near its best level in recent years, provision coverage above 200%, and real estate NPL ratio falling (4.85% to 4.20%) suggest the worst of property-related credit stress may be behind the bank

Implicit state support: as a G-SIB and majority state-owned bank with the Ministry of Finance as controlling shareholder (further increased via the placement), BOCOM carries very low perceived default/systemic risk, underpinning its low cost of capital and funding stability
bear_case: Earnings dilution from the 2025 placement is real and ongoing: EPS fell in both FY2025 (RMB1.16 to RMB1.08) and H1 2026 (-11.9% YoY) despite growing net profit, meaning per-share value creation has lagged headline profit growth and will take several years of profit growth to fully absorb

Structurally the weakest NIM among China's big banks (1.20-1.23%), leaving less buffer against further policy rate cuts or competitive deposit pricing pressure than larger, more retail-deposit-rich peers

Real estate and local-government-debt exposure remains a live risk despite improvement — RMB515bn in real-estate loans at a 4.2% NPL ratio and an explicit management acknowledgment that these sectors require ongoing 'monitoring, investigation and resolution'

Retail/personal loan asset quality continues to deteriorate (NPL ratio up to 1.58%, credit card NPL 2.68%), a trend management itself flags as a 'major concern of capital market' and one consistent with broader Chinese household balance-sheet stress

Low single-digit profit growth (net profit +2.18% FY2025, ROE declining from 10.76% in FY2021 to 8.09% in H1 2026) limits re-rating potential absent a more decisive NIM recovery or faster fee-income growth, and the bank remains subject to state-directed lending priorities that may not always maximize risk-adjusted shareholder returns
